founding_year.basis: Founded 2004 by Josh Kopelman with Howard Morgan; the first fund vehicle, First Round Capital 2005 LP, registered with the SEC on 2004-12-02 (CIK 1310616), which corroborates the year.

history.value: First Round Capital was founded in 2004 by Josh Kopelman, who had sold Half.com to eBay, with Howard Morgan. It led Uber's $1.25M angel round in 2010 and was an early investor in Square, Roblox, Warby Parker, Notion and Flexport. It invests from Philadelphia, New York and San Francisco, and its tenth fund closed at $500M in 2025.
history.basis: Assembled from the run's own evidence: the ADV (CRD 160848), the fund ladder's Form D filings, the firm's four site generations 2007-2026, and the landed base's own distribution. The two exclusions named in the last sentence are decisions.md D-T2a and D1. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). Not counted in the portfolio: the founders' pre-2005 angel investments (del.icio.us, IronPort, Flock, Feedster), which the firm itself lists as made before First Round Capital, and Dorm Room Fund, which runs on its own management company (decisions.md D-T2a and D1).

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from its homepage headline (h1, 'Beginnings Matter'), read 2026-09-26; sentence case, straight quotes and a closing period are the only edits. PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26). Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: Derived from the landed entry_stage distribution: Seed 509 (86%), Series A 59, Pre-Seed 22, Growth 4. The firm's own per-company label carries the same three values (Seed / Pre-Seed / Series A). Growth appears only where the record names a later round and is not part of the firm's stated remit, so it is not published as a stage.

investment_geo.basis: 553 of 594 rows are US (93%); the remainder is a long tail of nine countries with at most nine rows each (CA 9, GB 8, JP 5). One core label, no secondary — the two-label cap is not reached.

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 274 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 20 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: Median: the entry-round amount on the first Form D of 70 membership-verified base companies with filing histories — p25 $2.0M, median $5.74M, p75 $11.3M — published as $6M. This is a ROUND-SIZE proxy for cheque size and is fair only because First Round leads or co-leads most of the seeds it enters; the firm's own cheque is a fraction of it. Lower limit: the Pre-Seed entries, whose Form D rounds start at $0.5M. Upper limit: the largest verified entry rounds sit in the $20-30M band and the concentration cross-check agrees — 10-15% of the $500M flagship would be $50-75M for a whole position across follow-ons, not a first cheque.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first: the names a general reader would recognise first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Each is tied to its portfolio row by `slugs`; names read as a reader knows them, without legal suffixes (COLLECTION.md §8). Previously listed (10): Uber, Square, Roblox, Notion, Warby Parker, Flexport, Verkada, Ring, Blue Apron, Looker.

aum.basis: FR Capital Holdings, LP is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER (SEC 802-75765, CRD 160848, ERA since 2012-03-30), so no Item 5.F regulatory AUM exists. The sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B: 22 private funds, ALL reported as venture capital funds, with total gross assets of $3,843,440,251 on the annual amendment filed 2026-03-31. Both range ends are that one sworn number; no press figure above it is on the record. Note that the ADV ANONYMISES its funds under rule 204-2(d) — they appear as FUND 006 … FUND 030 with GPs as GP 004 — so the fund list below comes from Form D and press, not from the ADV.

funds.basis: The flagship ladder. Sizes for Funds III through X are the total offering amount on each vehicle's own Form D and are asserted against the accession at build time. The 2005, 2006, 2007 and II vintages filed Form D on PAPER (REGDEX only on EDGAR), so no sworn size exists for them: Fund II's $132.5M and the two annex funds' $5M and $15M are press figures, and the three earliest flagships carry null. The matching Partners Funds (the employee co-invest vehicles, $2.7M-$16M each), the -A and -F sleeves and the X-F vehicle are counted in the adviser's 22 but are not listed beside their flagships. The accession is recorded in each entry's source note rather than in the assertable field: First Round files the FULL fund size as the total-offering amount and amends at close, so the filing's `sold` is the close state on the filing date and not the fund size — the same filing style Lightspeed and Benchmark both required a note for (§11).

individuals.basis: Live team CMS: 19 members. Positions are CMS titles (13 explicit); untitled members under the investing tabs render as 'Partner', the site's own presentation. 2 names from the 2026 Wayback roster are no longer on the live team page. Socials from profile pages: 0 LinkedIn, 0 X.

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 2400 Market St, Suite 237, Philadelphia, PA (FR CAPITAL HOLDINGS, LP, CRD 160848, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31). The firm's site lists San Francisco, CA; New York, NY; Philadelphia, PA; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
